blocks.text: Dear Ms. Horne:

This letter sets out the terms on which we will carry out the actuarial valuation of the pension plan sponsored by Howard and Sons, and it asks for your signature so the work can begin. It follows our conversation this spring. We have put in writing what we will do, who will do it, and the basis on which we will do it, so that there is a shared record to return to as the engagement runs its course.
The Work We Are Engaged To Do

We will perform a full actuarial valuation of the plan as of its valuation date, measuring the plan's liabilities and its funded position and setting out the funding that follows from them. The work will be performed under the Actuarial Standards of Practice that apply to a valuation of this kind. We keep three things apart in everything we deliver: what the data show, what we have assumed, and what we conclude. You should be able to read a result and see which of the three it rests on.

The report itself is organized the same way we think. What the data show comes first, on its own. The assumptions and methods come next, stated so that a reader can see each one and weigh it. Our conclusions come last, and they rest visibly on the two sections above them. Nothing in the report asks you to take a judgment on faith.
The engagement has four parts, and the report will document each of them:

items: The participant census and asset information that you provide, which we reconcile and rely upon, with that reliance stated plainly in the report.
The plan provisions as set out in the current plan document, valued as they are written.
The actuarial assumptions and methods, which we set out on their own so they are never confused with the measured results.
A written report and a workbook of supporting exhibits, which together let a reader trace every number to its source.

blocks.text: Our Reliance on Your Data

A valuation is only as sound as the records it is built on. We will rely on the census and asset data your office provides, and we will reconcile it before we use it. Where a record is unclear, we will come back to you rather than guess. We do not audit the data, and we say so in the report; what we do is check it for internal consistency and against the prior year, and document what we relied on.
The People on the Engagement

Jennifer Vasquez, a consulting actuary in our firm, will lead the engagement day to day and will be your point of contact for the questions that come up as we go. David Sherman, a senior analyst, will build and reconcile the valuation workbook and document the data we rely on. Jeffrey Ochoa, an actuarial analyst, will carry the modeling and chase down anything in the results that needs explaining. I will review the work and sign the actuarial opinion. The professional responsibility for what we conclude is mine.
When the Work Begins

Subject to your signature on this letter, we will begin the work on {{fact:f:E-2016-001.start}}. Our first step is to request the census and asset records and to confirm the plan provisions we are to value. We will keep you informed of where the work stands, and we will not let a question sit quietly on our side when a short note to you would settle it.
Fees and Payment

Our fee for the engagement, and the basis on which it is set, are stated on the signature page, which counsel for each side has executed separately; they are not repeated here. We invoice monthly for the prior month's work, and each invoice is due within thirty days of its date. If a question about an invoice arises, tell us and we will work it through before it becomes a dispute.
Term and Ending the Engagement

This agreement takes effect on the date you sign below and continues until we deliver the valuation and you have paid our final invoice for it. Either of us may end it earlier on written notice to the other. If the engagement ends before the valuation is complete, you will owe us for the work done up to that point, and we will hand over what we have in a usable form.
Confidentiality

We will hold what you give us in confidence and use it only for this engagement. Within the firm, access is limited to the people named above and to those whose work on the valuation requires it. We will not disclose your information outside the firm without your consent, except where the law or our professional standards require it, and in that event we will tell you unless we are barred from doing so.
The Limit of Our Liability

Our liability to you arising out of this engagement, whether framed in contract or in negligence, will not exceed the total fees you pay us under it, except in the case of our fraud or willful misconduct. Neither of us will be liable to the other for indirect or consequential loss. Any claim must be brought within one year of the delivery of the report.
Governing Law

This agreement is governed by the law of the state in which our office sits, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules. Before either of us begins a proceeding, we will try to resolve the matter through discussion between people with authority to settle it.

If these terms match your understanding, please sign both copies where shown, keep one for your records, and return the other to me. If anything here does not read the way you expected, call me before you sign and we will settle it. We are glad to be doing this work for you, and we will give it the care it deserves.
Sincerely,

To: David Sherman, Jeffrey Ochoa, Carol Cooper
From: Jennifer Vasquez
Re: Howard and Sons pension valuation
Objective

This memo sets the plan for the {{fact:f:E-2016-001.client}} pension valuation. The objective is a full actuarial valuation of the plan and a report the client's board can act on. The deliverables are the report and a workbook of exhibits that supports it.

The valuation measures the plan's liabilities and its funded position as of the valuation date, on the funding basis and the accounting basis. It is performed under the applicable Actuarial Standards of Practice. We keep measurement, assumption, and conclusion separate in the report, as we always do.
Our point of contact is Elizabeth Horne, Director of Operations. Data requests and scheduling go through her office. Client-facing questions come to me before they go to her.
Assignments

items: Data. David Sherman reconstructs the participant census and the asset records, reconciles both, and documents our reliance. He ties the headcount and the assets to the prior year and to the client's own summaries, and flags any gap before anything is modeled.

Modeling. Jeffrey Ochoa builds the valuation model and prepares the assumption inputs for review: the interest rate, mortality, and the retirement and termination rates. He sets no assumption as final until it has been reviewed, and he traces any surprising result back to the input that produced it.

Client relationship. I hold the scope calls and the contact with Elizabeth Horne. I own the questions the board wants answered and the harder job of saying which of them the data can answer and which it cannot.
Scheduling. Carol Cooper tracks the data requests and the delivery date against the board's calendar, and keeps the open items visible so nothing waits on a request no one has sent.

blocks.text: What the Work Depends On

Two things gate the rest. The first is a clean confirmation of the plan provisions we are to value, against the current plan document. The second is complete census and asset data. Until both are in hand, we set assumptions provisionally and value nothing.

Data quality is the usual risk on a first valuation for a client. Expect the census to need a pass for status codes and for participants whose records do not agree with the summary. We raise those with Elizabeth Horne early rather than carry them into the model.
The First Two Weeks
Work begins on {{fact:f:E-2016-001.start}}. I will send the data request to Elizabeth Horne this week. It will list the census fields and the asset statement we need, with the format we want them in.

David Sherman loads the census as soon as it arrives and reports any gap the same day. Jeffrey Ochoa drafts the assumption memo for my review before any assumption is treated as settled. We do not value the plan until the plan document and the data are both confirmed.
Carol Cooper will circulate the schedule once the data request is out, mapped to the board's meeting dates so the draft and the final report land where the board can use them.

To: Elizabeth Horne
Cc: David Sherman, Jeffrey Ochoa
Hi Elizabeth,

This note opens our working thread for the {{fact:f:E-2016-001.client}} pension valuation. We have started. David Sherman is reconstructing the participant census from the file your office sent last week, and Jeffrey Ochoa is setting up the valuation model.

Two items from your side will keep us on schedule. We need your confirmation that the plan provisions we are to value match the current plan document at Howard and Sons, and the most recent asset statement whenever it is to hand. Neither is urgent this week.
Please keep this thread as our record for the data and the assumptions. Questions sent here reach the whole team at once.
Sincerely

To: Elizabeth Horne
Cc: Jennifer Vasquez, David Sherman
Good morning Elizabeth,
The census file for the {{fact:f:E-2016-001.client}} plan is usable, and the headcount ties to your summary. David Sherman reconciled it yesterday and it agrees line for line.

One field needs a definition before we rely on it. The file groups a set of participants under a status code we cannot read with confidence. Could you confirm how it distinguishes active participants from deferred vested ones? Once we have that, the census for the Howard and Sons plan is settled on our end, and nothing about the assumptions is locked before you have seen it.
Thanks

To: Elizabeth Horne
Cc: David Sherman, Jeffrey Ochoa
Hi Elizabeth,

Following Jeffrey Ochoa's note, one point on scope. We will value the plan provisions exactly as they are written in the current plan document at Howard and Sons. Your confirmation of that document is the item that unblocks the rest.
On the asset side, the most recent custodian statement is what we need, whenever it is available. There is no rush this week. David Sherman will fold it into the workbook when it arrives.
Nothing is being valued yet. We hold the {{fact:f:E-2016-001.client}} numbers until the plan document and the data are both confirmed.
Sincerely

To: Elizabeth Horne
Cc: Jennifer Vasquez, David Sherman
Good morning Elizabeth,
That clears the last open item on the data side, and we can proceed. With the status codes defined, the census for the Howard and Sons plan is complete and reconciled.

When the asset statement reaches us, I will reconcile it against the plan's records, and Jennifer Vasquez will confirm the assumption set before we run the first cut of the {{fact:f:E-2016-001.client}} valuation. You will see the assumptions before any results.
Thanks
